All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR re…

## PR Description

Closes #1036
### What changed
Brought both CRAP-target functions under 30 by extracting pure helpers and pinning behaviour with characterization tests: `buildFactoryState` **65 → 13** (CC, 100% cov) and `normalizeTicket` **39 → 11** (CC, 100% cov). No behaviour change — same exports/signatures, same snapshot key order, same cite/carry semantics.

### Key decisions
- `normalizeTicket` is now a thin decide-dispatch over per-provider parse helpers (`_normalizeFlatTicket` / `_normalizeJiraTicket` / `_normalizeAdoTicket` / `_normalizeGithubTicket` + tiny `_nameOf` / `_parentKeyOf` / `_adoKey` / `_githubKey`), all inside the existing `createTracker` closure — no export or signature changes.
- `buildFactoryState`'s verdict/cite closure cluster moved top-level (`headVerdict`, `citeFromPool`, `citeTier`, `runCite`, `freshestRun`, …) with identical tier/cancelled/auxiliary semantics; the issue loop, PR/merged card builders, backlog cap, latch carry and the state shell became small pure helpers (`issueEntry`, `openPrCard`, `mergedChecksFor`, `mergeLatchCarry`, `buildState`, …), all exported for direct testing (additive exports only).
- `state` keeps the exact schema 2 top-level key order (`schema, factory, repo, tick, checks, …`) — pinned by a characterization test.
- Removed only the one-line `isRealRun` closure wrapper (inlined as `isValidationRun(r, ciWorkflow)` calls). CRAP ratchet diff: 0 functions up, 5 down, no new function > 8.
- New characterization suites pin per-provider `normalizeTicket` output shapes and `buildFactoryState` snapshot/card behaviour before and after the extraction, plus direct unit tests for every extracted helper (incl. previously uncovered merged-PR-with-head path).

# gh-1036: [CRAP] factoryState.buildFactoryState (65) + common/trackers.normalizeTicket (39)

## Description

## Problem
`js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState` **65** builds the factory board snapshot; `js/common/trackers.js::normalizeTicket` **39** is used by every tracker. Both are shared, so pin current output with characterization tests first.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

Now let me read the changed source files in full, especially factoryState.js, to check for subtle behavior changes.

2. `runCite` — original: `runVerdictOf` inlined as `var done = r.status === 'completed'`. New splits into `runVerdictOf` and `runConclusionOf`. Behavior: `verdict: done ? (r.conclusion || r.status) : r.status`, `conclusion: done ? (r.conclusion || null) : null`. Same.
3. `headVerdict` — original: `headRuns(sha)` closure over `runs`; new takes `runs` param. `isRealRun` inlined. Same tier logic: `[2,1].forEach` with `if (cite) return`. Same.
4. `issueEntry` — important behavior check: original computed `devStartedAtByIssue[it.number]` inside `if (inDev)` and used it in twinExtra check `if (devStartedAtByIssue[it.number])`. New: `var devStartedAt;` only set inside `if (inDev)`, and twinExtra checks `if (devStartedAt)`. Original devStartedAtByIssue only set when inDev too. So equivalent.

Wait — one subtle difference: original order of operations. Original:
```
var inDev = ...
var bucket = ...
if (hasLabel(DEV_DONE) && bucket !== 'blocked') return;
var prevCard = ...
if (inDev) { devStartedAt carry logic }
issueHistory[...] = nextHistory(...)
if (inDev) { lanes.development.push }
twin...
```
New issueEntry:
```
if inDev computed, bucket computed, devDone check, prevCard
issueHistory set FIRST, then devStartedAt carry, then push
```
Order of nextHistory vs devStartedAt — no dependency. Fine.

5. `openPrCard` — same fields. Original `_now: now` set, then delete. Same.
6. `mergedPrCard` — same. Note in original, `mergedChecks` was computed from `prevCard` which is `pix.pr[pr.number]`. New `mergedChecksFor(pr, pix.pr[pr.number], verdictFor)`. Same.
7. `buildState` — Object.keys(body).forEach appends body keys. Body key order: in buildFactoryState call, `body` object literal: `checks, reworkInFlight, zombiesSwept, lanes, counts, backlog, backlogCounts`. Original state literal had same order. Same.

Wait — original: `counts` computed via LANE_ORDER reduce and `backlogCounts`. New same via helpers. Good.

8. exports — additive, fine.

9. trackers.js normalizeTicket — check equivalence:
- Flat: same.
- Jira: `f.status && f.status.name ? ... : null` → `_nameOf(f.status)`. `f.issuetype && ...` → `_nameOf`. `f.parent && f.parent.key` → `_parentKeyOf`. Same.
- ADO: `_adoKey(t)` = `t.id != null ? String(t.id) : null` — called twice, same as original twice. Same.
- GitHub: `_githubKey(t)` — original: `owner && repo ? owner+'/'+repo+'#'+t.number : (t.key != null ? String(t.key) : '#'+t.number)`. New identical. Same.

One potential issue: the tests use `jira.normalizeTicket` for ADO/GitHub shapes — but normalizeTicket dispatch doesn't depend on provider, fine.

10. Test coverage of `_normalizeFlatTicket` etc.? The characterization test in test_trackers covers all branches through normalizeTicket, fine.

The new top-level headVerdict uses `isValidationRun(r, ciWorkflow)` and `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` and `isValidationWorkflowPath` — these must be top-level functions/constants in the module. Let me verify they exist at top level (previously used inside closures, but they were likely module-level). Let me check.

Also check `hasLabel`, `backlogBucket`, `issueCard`, `nextHistory`, `iso`, `laneOf`, `mergeLabelTimestamps`, `carryTimestamps`, `BACKLOG_CAP`, `BACKLOG_BUCKETS`, `MERGED_WINDOW_MS`, `LANE_ORDER`, `DEV_LABEL`, `DEV_DONE_LABEL` — all must be module-level. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1052
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1052
- **Title**: gh-1036 [CRAP] factoryState.buildFactoryState (65) + common/trackers.normalizeTicket (39)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1036` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +792
- **Deletions**: -293
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T15:46:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T15:46:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1036
### What changed
Brought both CRAP-target functions under 30 by extracting pure helpers and pinning behaviour with characterization tests: `buildFactoryState` **65 → 13** (CC, 100% cov) and `normalizeTicket` **39 → 11** (CC, 100% cov). No behaviour change — same exports/signatures, same snapshot key order, same cite/carry semantics.

### Key decisions
- `normalizeTicket` is now a thin decide-dispatch over per-provider parse helpers (`_normalizeFlatTicket` / `_normalizeJiraTicket` / `_normalizeAdoTicket` / `_normalizeGithubTicket` + tiny `_nameOf` / `_parentKeyOf` / `_adoKey` / `_githubKey`), all inside the existing `createTracker` closure — no export or signature changes.
- `buildFactoryState`'s verdict/cite closure cluster moved top-level (`headVerdict`, `citeFromPool`, `citeTier`, `runCite`, `freshestRun`, …) with identical tier/cancelled/auxiliary semantics; the issue loop, PR/merged card builders, backlog cap, latch carry and the state shell became small pure helpers (`issueEntry`, `openPrCard`, `mergedChecksFor`, `mergeLatchCarry`, `buildState`, …), all exported for direct testing (additive exports only).
- `state` keeps the exact schema 2 top-level key order (`schema, factory, repo, tick, checks, …`) — pinned by a characterization test.
- Removed only the one-line `isRealRun` closure wrapper (inlined as `isValidationRun(r, ciWorkflow)` calls). CRAP ratchet diff: 0 functions up, 5 down, no new function > 8.
- New characterization suites pin per-provider `normalizeTicket` output shapes and `buildFactoryState` snapshot/card behaviour before and after the extraction, plus direct unit tests for every extracted helper (incl. previously uncovered merged-PR-with-head path).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # canonical harness
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js js/unit-tests/test_trackers.js
```
Coverage/CRAP (same pipeline as `.github/workflows/quality.yml`):
```bash
nyc instrument --cwd . . /tmp/inst && rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ /tmp/inst/
node ci/run_with_coverage.js /tmp/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js /tmp/cov.json $FILES
crap4js . --coverage /tmp/cov.json --threshold 99999   # targets: 13 and 11
```

flowchart TD

  BFS --> IE[issueEntry]
  BFS --> OP[openPrCard / mergedPrCard]
  BFS --> MS[mergeLatchCarry + buildState]

  NT --> J[_normalizeJiraTicket]
  NT --> A[_normalizeAdoTicket]
  NT --> G[_normalizeGithubTicket]
```
</details>

## Description

Now let me read the changed source files in full, especially factoryState.js, to check for subtle behavior changes.

Key things to check:
1. `freshestRun` — original: sorts descending using runSortKey of b vs a. New: same, with `runSortKey` helper. But original had `(list || [])` guard and `String(...(b && ...) || '')`. New runSortKey does `String((r && (r.updated_at || r.created_at)) || '')`. Same.
2. `runCite` — original: `runVerdictOf` inlined as `var done = r.status === 'completed'`. New splits into `runVerdictOf` and `runConclusionOf`. Behavior: `verdict: done ? (r.conclusion || r.status) : r.status`, `conclusion: done ? (r.conclusion || null) : null`. Same.
3. `headVerdict` — original: `headRuns(sha)` closure over `runs`; new takes `runs` param. `isRealRun` inlined. Same tier logic: `[2,1].forEach` with `if (cite) return`. Same.
4. `issueEntry` — important behavior check: original computed `devStartedAtByIssue[it.number]` inside `if (inDev)` and used it in twinExtra check `if (devStartedAtByIssue[it.number])`. New: `var devStartedAt;` only set inside `if (inDev)`, and twinExtra checks `if (devStartedAt)`. Original devStartedAtByIssue only set when inDev too. So equivalent.

Wait — one subtle difference: original order of operations. Original:
```
var inDev = ...
var bucket = ...
if (hasLabel(DEV_DONE) && bucket !== 'blocked') return;
var prevCard = ...
if (inDev) { devStartedAt carry logic }
issueHistory[...] = nextHistory(...)
if (inDev) { lanes.development.push }
twin...
```
New issueEntry:
```
if inDev computed, bucket computed, devDone check, prevCard
issueHistory set FIRST, then devStartedAt carry, then push
```
Order of nextHistory vs devStartedAt — no dependency. Fine.

5. `openPrCard` — same fields. Original `_now: now` set, then delete. Same.
6. `mergedPrCard` — same. Note in original, `mergedChecks` was computed from `prevCard` which is `pix.pr[pr.number]`. New `mergedChecksFor(pr, pix.pr[pr.number], verdictFor)`. Same.
7. `buildState` — Object.keys(body).forEach appends body keys. Body key order: in buildFactoryState call, `body` object literal: `checks, reworkInFlight, zombiesSwept, lanes, counts, backlog, backlogCounts`. Original state literal had same order. Same.

Wait — original: `counts` computed via LANE_ORDER reduce and `backlogCounts`. New same via helpers. Good.

8. exports — additive, fine.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Now let me read the changed source files in full, especially factoryState.js, to check for subtle behavior changes.

2. `runCite` — original: `runVerdictOf` inlined as `var done = r.status === 'completed'`. New splits into `runVerdictOf` and `runConclusionOf`. Behavior: `verdict: done ? (r.conclusion || r.status) : r.status`, `conclusion: done ? (r.conclusion || null) : null`. Same.
3. `headVerdict` — original: `headRuns(sha)` closure over `runs`; new takes `runs` param. `isRealRun` inlined. Same tier logic: `[2,1].forEach` with `if (cite) return`. Same.
4. `issueEntry` — important behavior check: original computed `devStartedAtByIssue[it.number]` inside `if (inDev)` and used it in twinExtra check `if (devStartedAtByIssue[it.number])`. New: `var devStartedAt;` only set inside `if (inDev)`, and twinExtra checks `if (devStartedAt)`. Original devStartedAtByIssue only set when inDev too. So equivalent.

Wait — one subtle difference: original order of operations. Original:
```
var inDev = ...
var bucket = ...
if (hasLabel(DEV_DONE) && bucket !== 'blocked') return;
var prevCard = ...
if (inDev) { devStartedAt carry logic }
issueHistory[...] = nextHistory(...)
if (inDev) { lanes.development.push }
twin...
```
New issueEntry:
```
if inDev computed, bucket computed, devDone check, prevCard
issueHistory set FIRST, then devStartedAt carry, then push
```
Order of nextHistory vs devStartedAt — no dependency. Fine.

5. `openPrCard` — same fields. Original `_now: now` set, then delete. Same.
6. `mergedPrCard` — same. Note in original, `mergedChecks` was computed from `prevCard` which is `pix.pr[pr.number]`. New `mergedChecksFor(pr, pix.pr[pr.number], verdictFor)`. Same.
7. `buildState` — Object.keys(body).forEach appends body keys. Body key order: in buildFactoryState call, `body` object literal: `checks, reworkInFlight, zombiesSwept, lanes, counts, backlog, backlogCounts`. Original state literal had same order. Same.

Wait — original: `counts` computed via LANE_ORDER reduce and `backlogCounts`. New same via helpers. Good.

8. exports — additive, fine.

9. trackers.js normalizeTicket — check equivalence:
- Flat: same.
- Jira: `f.status && f.status.name ? ... : null` → `_nameOf(f.status)`. `f.issuetype && ...` → `_nameOf`. `f.parent && f.parent.key` → `_parentKeyOf`. Same.
- ADO: `_adoKey(t)` = `t.id != null ? String(t.id) : null` — called twice, same as original twice. Same.
- GitHub: `_githubKey(t)` — original: `owner && repo ? owner+'/'+repo+'#'+t.number : (t.key != null ? String(t.key) : '#'+t.number)`. New identical. Same.

One potential issue: the tests use `jira.normalizeTicket` for ADO/GitHub shapes — but normalizeTicket dispatch doesn't depend on provider, fine.

10. Test coverage of `_normalizeFlatTicket` etc.? The characterization test in test_trackers covers all branches through normalizeTicket, fine.

Now check: does anything else import these modules and could break due to added exports? Additive only, no.

Check `isValidationRun` and `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` are defined at module top-level in factoryState.js (used by new top-level functions). The new top-level headVerdict uses `isValidationRun(r, ciWorkflow)` and `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` and `isValidationWorkflowPath` — these must be top-level functions/constants in the module. Let me verify they exist at top level (previously used inside closures, but they were likely module-level). Let me check.

Also check `hasLabel`, `backlogBucket`, `issueCard`, `nextHistory`, `iso`, `laneOf`, `mergeLabelTimestamps`, `carryTimestamps`, `BACKLOG_CAP`, `BACKLOG_BUCKETS`, `MERGED_WINDOW_MS`, `LANE_ORDER`, `DEV_LABEL`, `DEV_DONE_LABEL` — all must be module-level. Since buildFactoryState was already using them, they're module-level. Fine.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1052
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1052
- **Title**: gh-1036 [CRAP] factoryState.buildFactoryState (65) + common/trackers.normalizeTicket (39)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1036` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +792
- **Deletions**: -293
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T15:46:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T15:46:51Z

## PR Description

Closes #1036
### What changed
Brought both CRAP-target functions under 30 by extracting pure helpers and pinning behaviour with characterization tests: `buildFactoryState` **65 → 13** (CC, 100% cov) and `normalizeTicket` **39 → 11** (CC, 100% cov). No behaviour change — same exports/signatures, same snapshot key order, same cite/carry semantics.

### Key decisions
- `normalizeTicket` is now a thin decide-dispatch over per-provider parse helpers (`_normalizeFlatTicket` / `_normalizeJiraTicket` / `_normalizeAdoTicket` / `_normalizeGithubTicket` + tiny `_nameOf` / `_parentKeyOf` / `_adoKey` / `_githubKey`), all inside the existing `createTracker` closure — no export or signature changes.
- `buildFactoryState`'s verdict/cite closure cluster moved top-level (`headVerdict`, `citeFromPool`, `citeTier`, `runCite`, `freshestRun`, …) with identical tier/cancelled/auxiliary semantics; the issue loop, PR/merged card builders, backlog cap, latch carry and the state shell became small pure helpers (`issueEntry`, `openPrCard`, `mergedChecksFor`, `mergeLatchCarry`, `buildState`, …), all exported for direct testing (additive exports only).
- `state` keeps the exact schema 2 top-level key order (`schema, factory, repo, tick, checks, …`) — pinned by a characterization test.
- Removed only the one-line `isRealRun` closure wrapper (inlined as `isValidationRun(r, ciWorkflow)` calls). CRAP ratchet diff: 0 functions up, 5 down, no new function > 8.
- New characterization suites pin per-provider `normalizeTicket` output shapes and `buildFactoryState` snapshot/card behaviour before and after the extraction, plus direct unit tests for every extracted helper (incl. previously uncovered merged-PR-with-head path).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # canonical harness
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js js/unit-tests/test_trackers.js
```

```bash
nyc instrument --cwd . . /tmp/inst && rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ /tmp/inst/
node ci/run_with_coverage.js /tmp/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js /tmp/cov.json $FILES
crap4js . --coverage /tmp/cov.json --threshold 99999   # targets: 13 and 11
```

```

blocks.text:
Now let me read the changed source files in full, especially factoryState.js, to check for subtle behavior changes.

Key things to check:
1. `freshestRun` — original: sorts descending using runSortKey of b vs a. New: same, with `runSortKey` helper. But original had `(list || [])` guard and `String(...(b && ...) || '')`. New runSortKey does `String((r && (r.updated_at || r.created_at)) || '')`. Same.
2. `runCite` — original: `runVerdictOf` inlined as `var done = r.status === 'completed'`. New splits into `runVerdictOf` and `runConclusionOf`. Behavior: `verdict: done ? (r.conclusion || r.status) : r.status`, `conclusion: done ? (r.conclusion || null) : null`. Same.
3. `headVerdict` — original: `headRuns(sha)` closure over `runs`; new takes `runs` param. `isRealRun` inlined. Same tier logic: `[2,1].forEach` with `if (cite) return`. Same.
4. `issueEntry` — important behavior check: original computed `devStartedAtByIssue[it.number]` inside `if (inDev)` and used it in twinExtra check `if (devStartedAtByIssue[it.number])`. New: `var devStartedAt;` only set inside `if (inDev)`, and twinExtra checks `if (devStartedAt)`. Original devStartedAtByIssue only set when inDev too. So equivalent.

Wait — one subtle difference: original order of operations. Original:
```
var inDev = ...
var bucket = ...
if (hasLabel(DEV_DONE) && bucket !== 'blocked') return;
var prevCard = ...
if (inDev) { devStartedAt carry logic }
issueHistory[...] = nextHistory(...)
if (inDev) { lanes.development.push }
twin...
```
New issueEntry:
```
if inDev computed, bucket computed, devDone check, prevCard
issueHistory set FIRST, then devStartedAt carry, then push

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Now let me read the changed source files in full, especially factoryState.js, to check for subtle behavior changes.

Key things to check:

2. `runCite` — original: `runVerdictOf` inlined as `var done = r.status === 'completed'`. New splits into `runVerdictOf` and `runConclusionOf`. Behavior: `verdict: done ? (r.conclusion || r.status) : r.status`, `conclusion: done ? (r.conclusion || null) : null`. Same.
3. `headVerdict` — original: `headRuns(sha)` closure over `runs`; new takes `runs` param. `isRealRun` inlined. Same tier logic: `[2,1].forEach` with `if (cite) return`. Same.
4. `issueEntry` — important behavior check: original computed `devStartedAtByIssue[it.number]` inside `if (inDev)` and used it in twinExtra check `if (devStartedAtByIssue[it.number])`. New: `var devStartedAt;` only set inside `if (inDev)`, and twinExtra checks `if (devStartedAt)`. Original devStartedAtByIssue only set when inDev too. So equivalent.

Wait — one subtle difference: original order of operations. Original:
```
var inDev = ...
var bucket = ...
if (hasLabel(DEV_DONE) && bucket !== 'blocked') return;
var prevCard = ...
if (inDev) { devStartedAt carry logic }
issueHistory[...] = nextHistory(...)
if (inDev) { lanes.development.push }
twin...
```
New issueEntry:
```
if inDev computed, bucket computed, devDone check, prevCard
issueHistory set FIRST, then devStartedAt carry, then push
```
Order of nextHistory vs devStartedAt — no dependency. Fine.

5. `openPrCard` — same fields. Original `_now: now` set, then delete. Same.
6. `mergedPrCard` — same. Note in original, `mergedChecks` was computed from `prevCard` which is `pix.pr[pr.number]`. New `mergedChecksFor(pr, pix.pr[pr.number], verdictFor)`. Same.
7. `buildState` — Object.keys(body).forEach appends body keys. Body key order: in buildFactoryState call, `body` object literal: `checks, reworkInFlight, zombiesSwept, lanes, counts, backlog, backlogCounts`. Original state literal had same order. Same.

Wait — original: `counts` computed via LANE_ORDER reduce and `backlogCounts`. New same via helpers. Good.

8. exports — additive, fine.

9. trackers.js normalizeTicket — check equivalence:
- Flat: same.
- Jira: `f.status && f.status.name ? ... : null` → `_nameOf(f.status)`. `f.issuetype && ...` → `_nameOf`. `f.parent && f.parent.key` → `_parentKeyOf`. Same.
- ADO: `_adoKey(t)` = `t.id != null ? String(t.id) : null` — called twice, same as original twice. Same.
- GitHub: `_githubKey(t)` — original: `owner && repo ? owner+'/'+repo+'#'+t.number : (t.key != null ? String(t.key) : '#'+t.number)`. New identical. Same.

One potential issue: the tests use `jira.normalizeTicket` for ADO/GitHub shapes — but normalizeTicket dispatch doesn't depend on provider, fine.

10. Test coverage of `_normalizeFlatTicket` etc.? The characterization test in test_trackers covers all branches through normalizeTicket, fine.

The new top-level headVerdict uses `isValidationRun(r, ciWorkflow)` and `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` and `isValidationWorkflowPath` — these must be top-level functions/constants in the module. Let me verify they exist at top level (previously used inside closures, but they were likely module-level). Let me check.

Also check `hasLabel`, `backlogBucket`, `issueCard`, `nextHistory`, `iso`, `laneOf`, `mergeLabelTimestamps`, `carryTimestamps`, `BACKLOG_CAP`, `BACKLOG_BUCKETS`, `MERGED_WINDOW_MS`, `LANE_ORDER`, `DEV_LABEL`, `DEV_DONE_LABEL` — all must be module-level. Since buildFactoryState was already using them, they're module-level. Fine.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR re…

## PR Description

Closes #1036
### What changed
Brought both CRAP-target functions under 30 by extracting pure helpers and pinning behaviour with characterization tests: `buildFactoryState` **65 → 13** (CC, 100% cov) and `normalizeTicket` **39 → 11** (CC, 100% cov). No behaviour change — same exports/signatures, same snapshot key order, same cite/carry semantics.

### Key decisions
- `normalizeTicket` is now a thin decide-dispatch over per-provider parse helpers (`_normalizeFlatTicket` / `_normalizeJiraTicket` / `_normalizeAdoTicket` / `_normalizeGithubTicket` + tiny `_nameOf` / `_parentKeyOf` / `_adoKey` / `_githubKey`), all inside the existing `createTracker` closure — no export or signature changes.
- `buildFactoryState`'s verdict/cite closure cluster moved top-level (`headVerdict`, `citeFromPool`, `citeTier`, `runCite`, `freshestRun`, …) with identical tier/cancelled/auxiliary semantics; the issue loop, PR/merged card builders, backlog cap, latch carry and the state shell became small pure helpers (`issueEntry`, `openPrCard`, `mergedChecksFor`, `mergeLatchCarry`, `buildState`, …), all exported for direct testing (additive exports only).
- `state` keeps the exact schema 2 top-level key order (`schema, factory, repo, tick, checks, …`) — pinned by a characterization test.
- Removed only the one-line `isRealRun` closure wrapper (inlined as `isValidationRun(r, ciWorkflow)` calls). CRAP ratchet diff: 0 functions up, 5 down, no new function > 8.
- New characterization suites pin per-provider `normalizeTicket` output shapes and `buildFactoryState` snapshot/card behaviour before and after the extraction, plus direct unit tests for every extracted helper (incl. previously uncovered merged-PR-with-head path).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # canonical harness
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js js/unit-tests/test_factoryState.js js/unit-tests/test_trackers.js
```

# gh-1036: [CRAP] factoryState.buildFactoryState (65) + common/trackers.normalizeTicket (39)

## Description

## Problem
`js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState` **65** builds the factory board snapshot; `js/common/trackers.js::normalizeTicket` **39** is used by every tracker. Both are shared, so pin current output with characterization tests first.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.
